title: Shouldn't those with a content model of "Nothing" not render their children unless stated otherwise?
body:
[Looking at this demo](https://flems.io/#-sA7ncPw89Qgpfhc2h91DdDGByItqhB-idAeFobDYBBKtU--DgjxbVzQpAiFPcEjALA22VDtYkMWZZz7JFXAoyZCKrOkfAQNlyFIJBOUCf1CC43kvUIXiAxvMESMhAxpCgcwKEWYkqJ1cJxMkmFiUqbs+CKeUb2OCSpOJW9g07OJxNkuNxL00j9kSYllmMwtLOWMtaSKRAL2IjN7wMchiRAmQbKBTzvL4YcIyKJIICpEIADUVzXGx-IbPgzNExASVtRBfPCZKbRKTJMtS7QXEkSAYAQeLuHQXkAE5UAAdlJEAAF9CH4CNRAwAArbhiGkWQ4PgURWEWPgSpkDwBCQJAzzAeAAAoioASg8YAXA8Dxl1IDxB16jw-), I see that `<option>` basically just renders `option.textContent`, `<base>`, `<hr>`, `<source>`, `<track>`, and `<area>` render as if they had a content model of "Transparent", and the rest ignore their children.

The first and third make sense, but the second doesn't, especially for `<hr>` (which is valid in that context).
